theme: Housing supply and investor activity: building permits, Redfin investor purchases, mortgage rates, county assessor/parcel data, LLC ownership, NYC PLUTO/ACRIS
queries_run: gh search repos "parcel data llc ownership"

candidates.name: fitnr/acris-download
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tool + SQL schema (mysql.sql, postgres.sql, sqlite.sql) that downloads NYC's ACRIS real-estate transaction records (deeds, mortgages, liens, party names/entities on every recorded document) from the NYC Open Data portal and loads them into a database. No data files committed, but the schema is ready-made for parsing entity/LLC names on deed and mortgage documents. 69 stars, updated 30 Jul 2026 (active).
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap 13 (housing supply/LLC ownership) and the theme's ACRIS ask: ACRIS party names are the standard way to identify LLC-shell buyers of NYC real estate, a proxy for investor purchase activity and STR-conversion housing supply in the largest ABNB market for domestic urban nights.
candidates.size_hint: code + SQL schema only, no committed data rows; pulls from full ACRIS history (1966-present) via NYC Open Data API

candidates.name: talos/acris-bigquery
candidates.what_it_holds: Scripts to pull the same NYC ACRIS dataset from NYC Open Data and load it into BigQuery for faster querying (no rows committed to repo).
candidates.why_useful: Same ACRIS/LLC-ownership use case as acris-download but at BigQuery scale, useful if the team wants to run entity-name matching (LLC clustering) across the full ACRIS history without local DB setup.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same underlying NYC ACRIS source as fitnr/acris-download

candidates.name: talos/acris-schema
candidates.what_it_holds: Standalone Postgres schema definition for ACRIS legals/parties/documents tables (companion to acris-bigquery), no data.
candidates.why_useful: Reference schema for building an ACRIS ingestion pipeline if the team wants to roll their own rather than use fitnr's tool.

candidates.name: ezramechaber/acris-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: A scraper targeting ACRIS (recently updated 8 Sep 2026, actively maintained), 6 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Another live ACRIS access route in case fitnr's tool is stale or the NYC Open Data API schema shifts; worth checking for any committed sample data given the recent update.

candidates.name: clhenrick/nyc-property-extractor
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js app providing a map-based interface to query NYC's MapPLUTO (parcel/zoning/building attributes) and ACRIS (transaction) datasets together.
candidates.why_useful: Combines the two datasets the theme keyword hints named explicitly (PLUTO + ACRIS); useful as a reference implementation for joining parcel characteristics to ownership-transfer records for STR-supply analysis in NYC.
candidates.size_hint: app code, queries live NYC Open Data/Socrata endpoints, no bulk data committed
candidates.time_coverage: current PLUTO/ACRIS vintages as of last update (2020)

candidates.name: ResidentMario/acris
candidates.what_it_holds: Notebook-style overview/exploration of the NYC Dept. of Finance ACRIS dataset(s), explaining schema and fields.
candidates.why_useful: Good as documentation/onboarding to the ACRIS schema (party roles, document types) before building an LLC-ownership extraction pipeline.

candidates.name: bn4uc/visualizing-nyc-housing
candidates.what_it_holds: Visualizations combining NYC ACRIS records with HMDA (Home Mortgage Disclosure Act) mortgage-application data, likely with some processed/joined extracts committed.
candidates.why_useful: Bridges ACRIS ownership-transfer data with HMDA mortgage-origination data in one NYC housing pipeline — relevant to both the LLC-ownership and mortgage-rate/lending threads of this theme.

candidates.name: ryansherby/RedfinScraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Actively maintained (100 stars, updated 2 Sep 2026) Python library that calls Redfin's unofficial 'Stingray' API to bulk-pull for-sale listings and sold-home records (configurable 1mo-5yr sold windows) by zip code. No data committed; requires user-supplied zip list. README explicitly warns of Redfin IP-ban risk for misuse.
candidates.why_useful: Most substantial Redfin access tool found; could be adapted to build a for-sale/sold-inventory and price time series (a housing-supply proxy for STR host economics) in markets Airbnb over-indexes on, though it does not natively flag investor/LLC buyers.
candidates.size_hint: code only; scrape volume limited by Redfin's own rate limits
candidates.time_coverage: current + trailing 1mo-5yr sold windows at scrape time (not historical archive)

candidates.name: Alireza-devX/redfin-data-pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: End-to-end batch ETL pipeline (likely built on Redfin's public 'Data Center' weekly/monthly market CSVs — median sale price, inventory, days-on-market by metro) rather than a scraper of listing pages.
candidates.why_useful: If it ingests Redfin's public Data Center exports (national/metro housing-market time series back to ~2012), it is a ready pipeline for a housing-supply/price series usable as an STR-host-economics control variable.
candidates.size_hint: pipeline code, 1 star; underlying Redfin Data Center files are large public CSVs pulled at run time, not committed
candidates.time_coverage: depends on Redfin Data Center vintage (~2012-present) if that is the source
candidates.geography: US metros (per Redfin Data Center coverage)

candidates.name: cfpb/hmda-platform
candidates.what_it_holds: Official CFPB open-source regtech platform (not itself the data): backend that ingests, validates and publishes Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) Loan Application Register (LAR) filings from lenders; points to the public HMDA Data Browser (https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/data-browser/) and public LAR/TS data dumps stored on S3 via its 'Data Publisher' service.
candidates.why_useful: HMDA is the authoritative, free, loan-level US mortgage-origination dataset (rates, loan amounts, geography, applicant/property type) back to the 1970s at aggregate level and ~2007+ at loan level via the modern platform — a genuine free mortgage-rate/lending-volume source for the housing-supply/investor-purchase thread (mortgage rates + county-level lending activity), reachable via the linked Data Browser/S3 dumps rather than this repo's own commits.
candidates.size_hint: platform source code only in this repo; external HMDA public LAR datasets run into tens of millions of loan records per year
candidates.time_coverage: modern HMDA platform ~2017-present; HMDA aggregate data back to 1975 via Data Browser

candidates.name: skonasani/Chicago-Permits-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Pipeline (SQL + Python via Socrata API) over the City of Chicago's public building-permits dataset, 236,847 records, with a dashboard on neighborhood-level permit-driven demand signals.
candidates.why_useful: Building-permit volume is a direct new-housing-supply proxy relevant to STR-host-supply growth in a major ABNB market (Chicago is in the team's 13-city Inside Airbnb panel); the Socrata ingestion code is reusable for other cities' open permit portals too.
candidates.size_hint: 236,847-row Chicago permits dataset (pulled live via Socrata, not necessarily committed as a static file)
candidates.time_coverage: per Chicago Data Portal permits dataset (2006-present typically)

candidates.name: amiriqbalkhan123/Data-Cleaning-San-Francisco-Building-Permits-Dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Cleaned/processed version of San Francisco's public building-permits dataset, ~198k records, with a semantic-normalization and validation pipeline.
candidates.why_useful: SF is a high-cost, high-regulation STR/housing market; a cleaned, analysis-ready 198k-row permits file is a usable new-housing-supply proxy with minimal further prep, if the cleaned CSV is committed in the repo.
candidates.size_hint: ~198,000 records (city of San Francisco building permits)

candidates.name: ampayreh/seattle-civic-data-tool
candidates.what_it_holds: Natural-language query tool that translates questions into Socrata SODA API calls against Seattle's open-data Building Permits dataset (LLM-assisted analysis layer on top).
candidates.why_useful: A working, generalizable client for pulling Seattle building-permit records on demand; the same SODA pattern extends to any other Socrata-hosted city permits/parcel dataset.
candidates.size_hint: tool/query code only, live API pulls, no bulk data committed

candidates.name: Fournogo/Austin-Building-Permits
candidates.what_it_holds: Small script scraping/aggregating the City of Austin's public building-permit dataset totals.
candidates.why_useful: Austin is in the team's own 13-city Inside Airbnb panel; a working pull method for Austin permit totals is a direct, cheap new-supply proxy for that market.
candidates.size_hint: script only, aggregates totals rather than storing raw rows

notes: gh search hit its 6-call budget quickly on generic terms ("parcel data llc ownership", "nyc pluto acris", "mortgage rates historical" all returned zero/irrelevant hits — GitHub's repo search does not index README prose well for these compound phrases). WebSearch was already exhausted session-wide (200/200) before this scout could use it, and github.com/search web pages then 429'd on WebFetch, so coverage of the LLC-ownership-parcel-data and dedicated mortgage-rate-dataset sub-threads is thin — a future scout with search budget should retry 'HMDA loan level data mirror', 'nationwide parcel data llc shell company', 'Redfin data center weekly housing market csv', and 'FHFA house price index github' directly. No repo found that already links institutional/LLC buyer identification to Redfin or county-assessor data specifically (the theme's 'investor purchases' and 'LLC ownership' asks are the weakest-covered parts of this pull); ACRIS tooling for NYC is the strongest single find and squarely fills gap 13. cfpb/hmda-platform is code, not data, but its linked public Data Browser/S3 dumps are a genuine free point-in-time-able mortgage dataset worth a dedicated follow-up pull (not a GitHub-hosted file, so out of scope for this cataloguing pass beyond flagging it).
